question: Hypothyroidism is caused by which of the following anti-tubercular drug -
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Ethionamide" -> "inhibits thyroid hormone synthesis" -> "decreased levels of T3 and T4" -> "hypothyroidism" -> 85%
CHAIN: "PAS" -> "interferes with thyroid function" -> "possible decrease in thyroid hormone production" -> "hypothyroidism" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Cycloserine" -> "unclear effect on thyroid function" -> "no established link to hypothyroidism" -> "hypothyroidism unlikely" -> 40%
CHAIN: "Pyrazinamide" -> "no direct effect on thyroid hormone synthesis" -> "hypothyroidism unlikely" -> 30%
analysis: Hypothyroidism can be caused by certain anti-tubercular drugs, with Ethionamide being the most well-documented among the options provided. Ethionamide inhibits thyroid hormone synthesis, leading to decreased levels of T3 and T4, which can result in hypothyroidism. While PAS may have some potential to interfere with thyroid function, the evidence is less direct and not as well-established as that for Ethionamide. Cycloserine and Pyrazinamide do not have a recognized link to hypothyroidism. Therefore, based on the consensus and the strongest evidence, Ethionamide is the most likely cause of hypothyroidism among the listed anti-tubercular drugs.
